name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District fundamentals lean roughly eighteen points Republican
Gallrein holds a massive financial edge over an underfunded Democratic opponent
Prediction markets price Republicans near ninety-six percent
Open seat after Massie's primary loss adds only minor GOP friction
model.rationale: The seat's deep Republican lean, the Democrat's minimal fundraising and cash position, and market pricing near ninety-six percent Republican all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat created by Massie's primary defeat.
model.watch: A late scandal, a surge of Democratic outside spending, or an unusually favorable midterm turnout environment could narrow what is otherwise a low-risk Republican seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's Fourth District is an open seat after Thomas Massie lost renomination, and Republicans remain heavy favorites to hold it. The district's partisan lean of roughly eighteen points toward the GOP gives Ed Gallrein a large structural advantage, and prediction markets price the Republican at about ninety-six percent. No general-election polling indicates the race is competitive.

Melissa Strange has raised little more than one hundred forty thousand dollars and enters the fall with minimal cash on hand, while Gallrein's primary campaign drew millions in candidate and outside spending. A Libertarian is also on the ballot but is unlikely to affect the outcome. The main residual uncertainty involves Republican primary-season friction carrying into the fall and turnout variation, but the seat remains firmly in Republican hands.
